instructions: Think about your child over the past month. For each moment, pick the ONE answer that sounds most like your child right now, even if more than one fits. There are no wrong answers: every choice is a strength.
frequency_stem: In the past month, how often does your child...

scenarios.prompt: A free afternoon with no plans. Your child is most likely to...

options.text: read, or write a story, a script or a comic
work on a strategy game, a code, or a brain teaser
draw, design something, or rearrange their room

scenarios.prompt: In a co-op class or youth group, your child comes alive during...

options.text: anything hands-on: labs, building, sports or active games
worship, choir, or anything with music and rhythm
small-group time and getting to know everyone

scenarios.prompt: On a camping trip or a long day outdoors, your child...

options.text: wanders off a little way and enjoys the quiet
names the birds, plants or tracks, or wants to look them up
asks big questions, like why God made the world the way He did

scenarios.prompt: When your child is upset about something, they usually...

options.text: talk it out, or write about it
do something physical: shoot hoops, build, or go for a run
go off alone and think it through

scenarios.prompt: On a long road trip, your child...

options.text: tracks the route, the miles or the time left
has music on and knows every word
watches the land change and points out animals and farms

scenarios.prompt: At church, your child is most drawn to...

options.text: the art, the building, or sketching during the sermon
the people, from the little kids to the older folks
the teaching, and asking hard questions about it afterward

scenarios.prompt: Late in the evening, your child is most likely to...

options.text: be deep in a book, or writing something of their own
be listening to music, playing, or making up songs
want to talk about God, purpose, or what is fair and right

scenarios.prompt: On family game night, your child...

options.text: figures out the best strategy and knows every rule
keeps everyone laughing and makes sure no one is left out
joins in, then wants time to themselves afterward

scenarios.prompt: Given a free Saturday and some supplies, your child would...

options.text: design something: a room layout, a sketchbook page, a model
build, repair or take apart something with real tools
work in the garden, train a pet, or explore the creek

scenarios.prompt: When friends come over, your child...

options.text: has everyone laughing at their stories and jokes
plans the fun and makes sure everyone feels welcome
heads outside with them: the woods, the barn or the backyard

scenarios.prompt: Handed a big project, your child...

options.text: breaks it into steps, a list or a schedule first
jumps in to build, test or try something
wants to know why it matters before they start

scenarios.prompt: On a quiet evening at home, your child is most likely to...

options.text: sketch, design, or work on something detailed
practice an instrument, sing, or make a playlist
journal, or sit and think things over

frequency.text: read, write, or tell stories for fun
enjoy puzzles, numbers, or figuring out how things work
draw, design, or picture how something will look before making it
build, fix, cook, or make things with their hands
sing, play music, or notice sounds and rhythms
help others, or bring people together
want time alone to think things through
notice, care for, or ask about plants, animals or the outdoors
ask big questions about God, life, or right and wrong
